plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves emerge the following spring and die back by early summer, giving rise to the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, from Britain through central Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall, rhizomatous perennial forming dense colonies topped with arching plumes of tiny yellow flower heads. It thrives in meadows, roadsides and prairies and is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to North America (eastern and central United States and Canada); naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Despite its reputation, goldenrod is rarely the cause of hay fever; its pollen is heavy and sticky and insect-carried, while the wind-borne pollen of ragweed blooming at the same time is the true culprit.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with strappy leaves and sturdy stems topped by umbels of frilly, wavy-petaled pink flowers that sparkle in sunlight. It is popular in warm, sunny borders and makes a long-lasting cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; cultivated in temperate gardens in the UK, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The petals have a glittering, crystalline sheen, which gave rise to the common name 'Guernsey lily' relatives and has made Nerine a favorite for late-season color when most other bulbs are dormant.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen small tree or large shrub with sickle-shaped gray-green phyllodes and fluffy, fragrant globular flower clusters. In Australia's late winter to early spring it bursts into bloom, brightening bushland and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
